title: Needlessly hidden primary navigation
summary: Hiding frequent top-level destinations behind generic menus or unlabeled icons reduces discoverability when there is enough space to show them.
problem: Users repeatedly spend interaction cost revealing destinations that could remain visible and stable.
use_when: Auditing desktop or wide layouts where core destinations are hidden without a space or focus rationale
avoid_when: Narrow screens require a disclosure transformation or the product intentionally prioritizes immersive content
rationale: Visibility should reflect frequency and importance.
Responsive collapse is not a reason to hide navigation everywhere.

signals: desktop primary navigation exists only behind generic menu icon
frequent destinations require extra reveal action with ample width
